Recorded Go2 CDR replay on an owner-confirmed disposable Linux VM

This completes the recorded_service_replay step of go2-camera-rehearsal.txt.
It does not replace that procedure's physical publisher, serial, firmware and
fresh challenge review. A checksum identifies bytes; it does not authenticate
an unauthenticated DDS publisher. Generated test streams never qualify as a
physical firmware corpus. Keep every recording and decoded video outside Git.

1. Preserve the successful recorder's complete raw-recording directory and its
   exact sealed plan.json. Never edit recording.json, rename/drop samples, repair
   timestamps, substitute another plan, or concatenate recordings. The supported
   corpus has 30–1800 bounded little-endian CDR samples of the original 360p
   Annex-B H264 layout. Receipt timestamps must strictly advance over 1–35 seconds.
   A format change, partial capture, ambiguous publisher or missing provenance
   remains pending. Decoding must yield at least 30 frames and 20 distinct frames.
   Preserve the physical challenge notes and prior native/container acceptance
   alongside this corpus; the replay does not certify those observations.

2. On the machine holding the plan's original saved provenance, create a private
   copy containing only those exact hash-matched records. Set the two paths:

     export GO2_PLAN=/absolute/path/to/plan.json
     export GO2_PROVENANCE=/absolute/path/to/new-provenance
     python3 - <<'PY'
     import hashlib,json,os,shutil
     from pathlib import Path
     plan=json.loads(Path(os.environ['GO2_PLAN']).read_text())
     out=Path(os.environ['GO2_PROVENANCE']);out.mkdir(mode=0o700)
     records={'firmware_record':plan['firmware_record'],**plan['records']}
     for name,record in records.items():
         assert name in {'firmware_record','device_info','installed_agent','camera_list','kernel_module','ros_interfaces','baseline_apps','recovery'}
         source=Path(record['path'])
         assert source.is_file() and not source.is_symlink()
         assert hashlib.sha256(source.read_bytes()).hexdigest()==record['sha256'],name
         shutil.copyfile(source,out/name)
     PY

   Transfer the sealed plan, this provenance directory and raw-recording to the
   reserved VM through the owner's existing approved file-transfer mechanism.
   Verify their hashes after transfer. Do not upload binaries/credentials/whole
   device state to a public artifact store. A missing original file must be
   recovered from the owner; never create a replacement observation.

3. Use a fresh operator-owned disposable Linux VM with no robot connection,
   passed-through devices, production workload or host-directory write mounts.
   The VM must already have the owner-installed v4l2loopback 0.15.4 module, its
   /dev/v4l2loopback control node, and an unused /dev/video128. This script does
   not install/load/unload modules, create a VM or alter a host service. If the
   approved VM lacks those prerequisites, stop and have its owner prepare it
   using the reviewed module source. Never run this on the physical companion.

   Required tools are the checkout's Go version, Python3, sudo, util-linux
   unshare, systemd-detect-virt, containerd/ctr, runc, statically linked busybox,
   and GStreamer h264parse,avdec_h264,videoconvert,fdsrc,fdsink. The existing
   fixture creates a temporary private containerd daemon; no system daemon is
   stopped or reconfigured. Reserve at least 2 GiB free for transient test binaries
   and evidence in addition to Go build cache and the bounded recording.

   Independently confirm the VM in its hypervisor inventory and local console.
   Preserve the VM name/owner, hypervisor record and these read-only observations:

     systemd-detect-virt --vm
     systemd-detect-virt --container
     cat /proc/sys/kernel/random/boot_id
     sudo -n cat /sys/class/dmi/id/product_uuid
     uname -a
     cat /sys/module/v4l2loopback/version
     test -c /dev/v4l2loopback && test ! -e /dev/video128 && test ! -L /dev/video128

   The container probe must report none/exit 1. Supported explicit VM kinds are
   kvm,qemu,vmware,oracle,microsoft,xen,parallels; a physical host, container,
   unavailable detector, empty/placeholder identity or unsupported VM stays pending.
   Enter the observed boot_id and product_uuid explicitly at step5 after checking
   them against this VM. A reboot invalidates this confirmation. Do not fabricate
   GITHUB_ACTIONS or RUNNER_ENVIRONMENT to bypass admission.

4. Use an owner-reviewed checkout containing test-go2-recorded-replay.py. Record
   git rev-parse HEAD and its clean status. As the ordinary VM user, prepare a
   new private directory without accessing any device:

     python3 .github/scripts/test-go2-recorded-replay.py prepare \
       --archive /absolute/path/to/raw-recording \
       --plan /absolute/path/to/plan.json \
       --provenance /absolute/path/to/new-provenance \
       --confirm-robot-serial EXACT_SERIAL_FROM_REVIEWED_PLAN \
       --output /absolute/path/to/new-prepared-replay

   Preparation verifies copied bytes again, all sample hashes/lengths/layouts,
   the sealed plan hash, exact robot and target identities, recorded camera
   inventory, ordered receipt times and all eight provenance hashes. It rejects
   unexpected archive members, symlinks, duplicate JSON keys and interrupted
   recordings. The original corpus is not modified. Physical acceptance stays
   not_run even when this mechanical validation passes.

5. Run the explicit VM entrypoint as its ordinary user, with noninteractive sudo
   already authorized by the VM owner for this disposable environment:

     python3 .github/scripts/test-go2-recorded-replay.py run \
       --prepared /absolute/path/to/new-prepared-replay \
       --confirm-robot-serial EXACT_SERIAL_FROM_REVIEWED_PLAN \
       --confirm-vm-boot-id EXACT_BOOT_UUID_CONFIRMED_ABOVE \
       --confirm-vm-product-uuid EXACT_PRODUCT_UUID_CONFIRMED_ABOVE

   The entrypoint checks VM identity before compilation and again at kernel
   mutation/cleanup boundaries. It runs the unchanged CDR bytes through the
   production parser and V4L2 writer, then captures with the production native
   service outside and inside an actual camera-entitled OCI task. It independently
   decodes the original H264 source and each capture to 640x360 RGB frame hashes.
   All captured content must match the recording in order, with at least 6 decoded
   frames and 3 distinct frames per capture; bounded drops/repeated kernel buffers
   are permitted. Real long-GOP corruption or insufficient decodable output fails,
   rather than substituting generated keyframes or relaxing the comparison.

   Require exit 0, replay_passed:true and normal plus all three controls in the new
   run-*/evidence.json. The normal log must contain three
   GO2_RECORDED_CAPTURE_VERIFIED markers and
   GO2_RECORDED_KERNEL_CONTAINER_VERIFIED. Historical CDR layout, wrong kernel
   pixel format and missing camera annotation controls must each fail their
   specific assertion. A timeout, skipped test, prerequisite/compile error or
   generic process failure does not count as a rejected regression.

6. Preserve run logs/evidence, replay.json, the exact corpus/plan/provenance and
   source hashes privately with the physical challenge review. Namespace drain
   must complete and cleanup must report removal of only this run's exact-label
   video128. Confirm video128 is absent afterward. If shutdown is interrupted or
   ownership/drain cannot be proved, the entrypoint retains its resources and
   records failure. Do not broadly delete nodes or kill host processes; return
   the disposable VM to its owner for disposal and retain the evidence.

   Only then may a human mark recorded_service_replay passed with these evidence
   paths. Other physical cases retain their own outcomes. This test does not
   cover physical DDS discovery, the live camera Manager's scheduling, another
   firmware format, another robot, or robot actuation.
